block.title: The lifter turns bn_add_words's carry loop into nanofil IR with no new instruction
block.p: experiments/ct-bn-add lifts OpenSSL's bn_add_words and bn_sub_words, and a control that branches on the carry, with the lifter of . The IR has no carry, so one adc becomes two additions, two unsigned comparisons and an or, and the carry goes round the loop as a phi. nanofil prints each comparison as cmp and setb, with no branch. The IR and the Prolog SaRCAsm prototype's effect table are unchanged, and 34 of the file's 47 instructions are looked up in that table as it is.

tr.td: bn_add_words and bn_sub_words under zegarmistrz, operands poisoned
leaky_add_words when a tainted store keeps its taint
bn_add_words, ns per word on 512 words

claim.p: The four builds give the same answer on the 18 runs of drive.ir that return, and the lifted IR passes difftest.sh, agree.sh, valid.sh and gate.sh without and with -O. A lifter that leaves out the second comparison of adc still passes those four checks and fails the comparison with the original assembly. Nothing proves that the lifted IR computes what the assembly computes.

Against Poison.v as it is on main, with no axiom: if the checked IR of bn_add_words or bn_sub_words returns on some contents of the two operands, its leak trace is the same on any other contents, for any buffer size and count. leaky_add_words stops with CannotBranch. The theorems are about the IR's leak trace, not about the machine code.

SaRCAsm's bn_add_words takes 45 ns for each word, 90 times the original, because it keeps adc and saves the flags with pushf and popf around four checks in each iteration. The original loop with four such pairs and no check takes 43 to 45 ns for each word. With lahf and sahf in the same places it takes 6.4 to 6.7 ns.

Upstream zegarmistrz lets leaky_add_words finish in the unoptimized lifted build, in 3 of 3 runs, as it does leaky_memcmp. In both, nanofil without -O stores a loaded secret to a stack slot and then stores the condition computed from it to the same slot, and the emulator's store rule clears a slot's taint at the second tainted store.

block.p: The next kernel in OpenSSL's file, bn_mul_add_words, needs the high half of a 64-bit product, which the IR's mul does not give. That would be a new IR instruction, and it is worth adding when C needs it and not for the lifter alone.
